name: rdkit-recap-terminal-fragments

plan.name: rdkit-recap-terminal-fragments
plan.task: Decompose a sanitized RDKit molecule into RECAP terminal fragments using rdkit.Chem.Recap.RecapDecompose and root.GetLeaves(), returning terminal leaf nodes keyed by canonical SMILES with attachment points represented as '*' atoms.
plan.scope: Input is an already parsed and sanitized RDKit Mol from a valid SMILES; callers must handle invalid/None Mol before calling. Output is the standard terminal leaf dictionary; immediate children and full descendants via root.children or root.GetAllChildren() are not the primary terminal result. A valid empty leaf dictionary is expected when no permitted cleavable bond exists, including ring-only molecules, charged/protonated forms, and cases rejected by the small-fragment filter.
plan.entrypoint: from rdkit import Chem; from rdkit.Chem import Recap; mol = Chem.MolFromSmiles(smiles); if mol is None: raise/handle invalid input; root = Recap.RecapDecompose(mol); leaves = root.GetLeaves()  # dict SMILES -> RecapHierarchyNode; list(leaves.keys()) are terminal fragment SMILES. Optional controls: RecapDecompose(mol, minFragmentSize=N, onlyUseReactions={...}).
plan.rationale: Removes confusion between immediate children, all descendants, and terminal leaves by documenting that GetLeaves() returns only leaf nodes keyed by canonical product SMILES. It covers '*' dummy labels, canonical keys, default small-fragment rejection, and minFragmentSize/onlyUseReactions controls, so users can obtain standard RECAP terminal fragments without reading RDKit source or misinterpreting hierarchy nodes as terminal fragments.
plan.construction: Direct packaging of the existing rdkit.Chem.Recap API from the provided source; no new algorithm or research extension. Delivery would include a SKILL.md focused on terminal-fragment retrieval, examples extracted from source-embedded unit tests, BSD-3-Clause attribution, and a compatible RDKit environment prerequisite. No runtime package is authored at this discovery stage.

evidence.claim: RecapDecompose(mol, allNodes=None, minFragmentSize=0, onlyUseReactions=None) returns a RecapHierarchyNode and uses canonical MolToSmiles(mol,1) as its registry key; it repeatedly applies the predefined reactionDefs SMARTS reactions and stores node children keyed by product SMILES.

RecapHierarchyNode.GetLeaves() returns a dictionary keyed by SMILES of leaf nodes, descending recursively only into non-terminal children via _gacRecurse(res, terminalOnly=True); GetAllChildren() returns all descendants, not just terminal leaves.

reactionDefs defines 12 bond-cleavage SMARTS: urea, amide, ester, amines, cyclic amines, ether, olefin, aromatic N-aliphatic C, lactam N-aliphatic C, aromatic C-aromatic C, aromatic N-aromatic C (noted as not part of the standard RECAP set), and sulphonamide.

With minFragmentSize=0 (default), products whose dummy-stripped SMILES equals '', 'C', 'CC', or 'CCC' are rejected; with minFragmentSize>0, products are rejected when explicit atom count minus '*' dummy count is below minFragmentSize.

Embedded unittest tests demonstrate valid empty leaves for default decomposition of 'CCCOCCC', ring-only cases such as 'C1CCCCO1', and charged/protonated cases including 'c1ccccc1[n+]1ccccc1' and 'C1CC1[NH+]C(=O)CC'; the example 'C1CC1Oc1ccccc1-c1ncc(OC)cc1' yields three terminal leaves, and 'CCCOCCC' with minFragmentSize=3 yields one leaf rather than empty.

The retrieved RDKit license is BSD 3-Clause, copyright 2006-2015 Rational Discovery LLC, Greg Landrum, Julie Penzotti and others, permitting redistribution with copyright notice, conditions, and disclaimer.
